findings.title: New non-default method `order()` on public interface breaks external implementations
findings.body: Adding `int order()` as an abstract method to the `CryptoProvider` interface is a binary and source incompatible change. Any third-party or external module that implements `CryptoProvider` (which is a public interface in the `keycloak-common` module) will fail to compile or get a `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime. This should be a `default` method with a sensible fallback value (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve backward compatibility.

findings.title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and written but results discarded
findings.body: Lines 114-115 (`ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger); ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);`) create encoder instances, write to them, but the results are never used. The actual encoding is performed on lines 117-121. This is dead code that causes unnecessary object allocations on every call to `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`. It appears to be a leftover from development/refactoring.

findings.title: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` does not return a BouncyCastle provider
findings.body: The method `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is whatever JCA provider backs the default keystore type (typically SUN or SunJSSE), not BouncyCastle. The method's contract (per the interface Javadoc: 'BouncyCastle security provider. Can be either non-FIPS or FIPS based provider') is violated. If any code path calls this method expecting BouncyCastle-specific capabilities, it will fail or behave incorrectly. Consider throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` like the other unsupported methods, or documenting why this approximation is acceptable.

findings.title: Silent selection among multiple providers may mask classpath misconfiguration
findings.body: Previously, having multiple `CryptoProvider` implementations on the classpath threw an `IllegalStateException`, alerting users to a misconfiguration. Now the highest-order provider is silently selected and the others are only logged at DEBUG level. In production environments where DEBUG logging is typically disabled, a misconfigured classpath (e.g., accidentally including both `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402`) will no longer produce any visible error, potentially leading to subtle security or behavioral issues that are hard to diagnose.

findings.title: `CryptoIntegration.init` called on every `AuthzClient.create()` may race with server-side initialization
findings.body: `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` is called unconditionally in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)`. If the authz-client JAR is used in the same JVM as a Keycloak server (e.g., in integration tests or embedded scenarios), and the authz-client's classloader only sees `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (order 100), there is a race: if the authz-client initializes first, the static `cryptoProvider` will be set to `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, and subsequent server-side `init` calls will be no-ops, leaving the server with a provider that throws `UnsupportedOperationException` for most operations. The init call should be guarded or the authz-client should use `setProvider` only if no provider is already set.
